text:
oncall-bot: paging @jamal (oncall) — elevated agent/actioncall rates detected in prod region-us-west-2, latency SLO breaches and client 502s. pls ack

jamal: acked. seeing a 4.8x increase in `action_call.invoke` across the fleet starting ~T-8m. error rate climbing, CPU on some serving hosts saturated. investigating root cause but we need live mitigation now.

sara: any customer-facing impact yet? metrics?

jamal: yes, sustained 95th latency > 1200ms for generation endpoints that also use structured-output parsing. Host errors ~1.6% of requests in the last 5m. Tenants with heavy agent workflows (internal flag set) impacted more.

kai: re: structured output — is the parsing step causing CPU pressure or is it the extra token generation?

jamal: both. structured-output responses include large JSON blobs; token count per response up ~3x for flagged workloads. parsing + validation adds CPU and memory churn server-side.

alex: recommended immediate mitigations (short list): 1) soft-cap/slow-path action calls globally; 2) disable function/toolcall parsing for low-tier plans; 3) force text-only model variant for requests that request structured-output; 4) increase rejection + 429 for excess KV-cache warming flows. We should pick 1+2 now.

maya: +1 to short list. can we do feature-flag toggle so we can revert quickly?

jamal: yes. ops API has feature flags: `ff.disable_actioncall_parsing` and `ff.softcap_actioncall_rate`. I can flip. plan: flip softcap to 1rps/tenant for 10m, then disable parsing for free/trial tenants.

ops-bot: command accepted — rolling feature-flag change requires two approvals. @sara please approve? (see diff below)

sara: approved. execute.

jamal: executing now.

```bash
# apply soft cap: per-tenant rate limit to 1 rps for action calls
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://ops-api.internal/featureflags/softcap_actioncall_rate \
  -d '{"value": "1rps", "scope":"per-tenant", "expires_in":"10m"}'
```

ops-bot: feature flag `softcap_actioncall_rate` set -> 1rps per tenant (staged) by jamal.

jamal: now disabling parsing for free/trial tiers.

```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://ops-api.internal/featureflags/disable_actioncall_parsing \
  -d '{"value": true, "target_tiers": ["free","trial"]}'
```

ops-bot: feature flag `disable_actioncall_parsing` set -> true for tiers [free, trial] (rolling).

liz: seeing immediate drop in host CPU on a few hx nodes. latency 95th down ~18% in the first 90s. nice.

kai: jamal, can you also flip routing to fallback text-only model for requests that explicitly request `structured_json`? we should avoid model-level stalls.

jamal: adding routing rule now. will map `format=structured_json` to `model-compat/text-only-v2` for the next 15m.

```yaml
# routing rule snippet
- match: request.query.format == "structured_json"
  action: route
  target: model-compat/text-only-v2
  ttl: 15m
```

ops-bot: routing rule applied (staged).

alex: creating a short internal status note for support and docs: mention that we imposed soft caps and disabled action-call parsing for free/trial while we stabilize. keep message concise.

support-bot: draft queued to #support-inbox: "We've temporarily limited action/tool calling and structured-output parsing for free/trial customers due to elevated API load. Paid customers not impacted by parsing disablement unless they hit new soft caps. Engineering is investigating — more updates in incidents channel."

maya: what's the rollback plan if this increases errors?

jamal: rollback: revert feature flags and routing back to prior state (ops CLI has `ops rollback-feature <flag>`). if errors increase after softcap, we can narrow scope to only tenants with the spike using tenant selectors.

sara: we should also create a short-term quota adjustment for a handful of heavy tenants rather than global softcap if they identify as the root cause. jamal, can you produce a list of top 10 tenants by actioncall volume?

jamal: on it. pulling top-ten now.

[~90s later]

jamal: top 10 list ready. 3 tenants account for ~58% of extra action calls. two of them are internal test tenants running runaway agents. recommending tenant-specific rate limits + support outreach.

sara: ok, apply tenant-specific hard cap for those 3 (10rps -> 1rps) and open a P1 ticket for customers to contact their account reps.

jamal: applying tenant caps.

```bash
# apply tenant caps
for T in tenant-123 tenant-451 tenant-872; do
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
    https://ops-api.internal/tenants/$T/limits -d '{"actioncall_rps": 1}'
done
```

ops-bot: tenant caps applied for [tenant-123, tenant-451, tenant-872].

liz: error rate trending down to baseline (1.7% -> 0.4%). overall latency improving. great.

alex: drafting external status post for affected customers (short, empathetic). putting in #customer-comm for review.

maya: also add a snippet in console notifications for tenants whose parsing was disabled. explain how to re-enable and where to request exception.

alex: done. message posted to #customer-comm for review.

jamal: incident record created: INC-2026-0099 (live mitigation: softcaps + parsing disable + routing fallback + tenant caps). tagging eng-oncall and eng-sre for postmortem.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-0099 created and assigned to jamal. escalation to eng-sre scheduled.

sara: good work. after stabilization, we schedule a rollback test and plan a follow-up postmortem. please add timelines and action items to the incident doc.

jamal: will do. final status: soft cap + tier parsing disable + tenant caps in place; observed recovery in latency and error rate. continuing to monitor 15m window.

liz: monitoring graphs look stable for now. I'll keep an eye on host metrics.

support-bot: support notification sent to affected accounts and help center note published with workaround and ETA.

alex: leaving handoff notes here. @sara — handing off monitoring and comms to you. I might jump back if patterns re-emerge.

sara: taking over. thanks team.

oncall-bot: last update in thread: 1999887888 — thread closed for active mitigation but monitoring continues. reopen if escalates.
